title: Windshield Frame Bracket Redesign — Issue 2: Extension to the Side Window Interface
abstract: Second issue of the windshield frame work, extending the drained bracket and revised sealing standard to the side window interface, where the same pocket geometry was found after the first issue had been in service for two years.

sections.reason: The first issue removed the water pocket at the windshield lower forward corner and the removal rate for windshields fell to prediction within eighteen months. Side window removals did not fall, and inspection of nine returned side window assemblies found the same moisture pattern at the aft lower corner, where the web carries a comparable pocket that the first issue never covered. The design office judged it better to extend the proven standard than to open a separate investigation.
sections.description: The drained bracket profile introduced at the first issue is applied to the side window aft lower corner, and the sealing standard, bead profile and cure requirement are extended to that interface unchanged. The side window web is replaced by a variant with the drain path moulded in rather than machined, which is a manufacturing simplification rather than a functional change. The windshield frame parts introduced by the first issue are carried over without modification, so an aircraft embodying both issues has one bracket family and one sealant across the whole flight compartment glazing.
sections.effects: Mass increase of one point four kilograms per side over the first issue standard. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable at web level. Removal and installation task times for the side window increase by about an hour for the sealing sequence. The flight compartment window limitation entry is reissued for the second time, and the parts catalogue figure gains a further item pair.
sections.embodiment_note: Design launched. Production cut-in is planned two quarters after the design freeze; retrofit will be offered at the next side window change so that no additional glazing removal is required.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis has closed and the change is launched. The remaining open item carried forward is whether the moulded drain path can be qualified on the existing web tooling or needs a new tool, which sets the cut-in date.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in two quarters after design freeze, subject to web tooling qualification
